# `cluster-fast`

```{image} ../_static/pipeline_cluster-fast.svg
:width: 100%
:class: no-scaled-link
:align: center
```

The vOTU clustering module identifies viral operational taxonomic units (vOTUs) by clustering vContigs using one of two primary methods based on user requirements: the default fast clustering protocol—which utilizes CheckV’s MEGABLAST-based approach (enabled by `clustering-fast`)—or the more sensitive, though computationally intensive, CD-HIT approach (enabled by `clustering-sensitive`). To ensure biological consistency and standardized taxonomic resolution, both methods adhere to the Minimum Information about an Uncultivated Virus Genome (MIUViG) guidelines, requiring a minimum of 95% average nucleotide identity and 85% alignment coverage.

To handle large-scale datasets on memory-constrained hardware, the module also supports an optional loss-free iterative clustering framework (enabled by `--cluster-iter` or `--clustering-iter`). By executing a binary tree reduction (tournament-style merger) across partitioned inputs before final pooling, this iterative mode circumvents the quadratic $O(N^2)$ memory scaling typical of exhaustive all-versus-all alignments, reducing peak Resident Set Size (RSS) by up to 34% (CD-HIT) and 47% (CheckV) without loss of taxonomic resolution.

```{image} ../_static/cluster-iter.svg
:width: 100%
:class: no-scaled-link
:align: center
```

## Quick Run

::::{tab-set}
:::{tab-item} Single Fasta

**`Conda`**

```bash
snakemake --sdm conda --use-conda --config module="cluster-fast" fasta="sample/contigs/contigs_simulated_viral_nonviral.fasta" outdir="sample/results" -j 16 --latency-wait 20
```

**`Apptainer`**

```bash
snakemake --sdm conda apptainer --config module="cluster-fast" fasta="sample/contigs/contigs_simulated_viral_nonviral.fasta" outdir="sample/results" -j 16 --latency-wait 20
```

**`HPC (PBS) (Conda)`**

```bash
EMAIL="youremail@protonmail.com"
snakemake --sdm conda --use-conda --config module="cluster-fast" fasta="sample/contigs/contigs_simulated_viral_nonviral.fasta" outdir="sample/results" -j 88 --latency-wait 20 --executor cluster-generic --cluster-generic-submit-cmd "qsub -N {log} -l nodes=1:ppn={threads} -l mem={resources.mem_mb}m -l walltime=120:00:00 -M $EMAIL -q cgsd -o qsub.log -e qsub.log -m a"
```

**`HPC (PBS) (Apptainer)`**

```bash
EMAIL="youremail@protonmail.com"
snakemake --sdm conda apptainer --config module="cluster-fast" fasta="sample/contigs/contigs_simulated_viral_nonviral.fasta" outdir="sample/results" -j 88 --latency-wait 20 --executor cluster-generic --cluster-generic-submit-cmd "qsub -N {log} -l nodes=1:ppn={threads} -l mem={resources.mem_mb}m -l walltime=120:00:00 -M $EMAIL -q cgsd -o qsub.log -e qsub.log -m a"
```

:::
::::

``` {admonition} Dry Run
:class: Tip
Use the `-n` flag with your command to perform a dry-run first, listing all analyses that will be performed 
```

## Configuration

- **`clustering-fast`:** Flag to run fast clustering using CheckV's MEGABLAST approach. If set to False, CD-HIT will be used. Proceed with caution as it can be extremely slow at large sequence numbers. (default: True)
- **`cdhit-params`:** Additional parameters to pass on to CD-HIT if clustering-fast is set to False <https://github.com/weizhongli/cdhit/blob/master/doc/cdhit-user-guide.wiki>. (default: "-c 0.95 -aS 0.85 -d 400 -M 0 -n 5")
- **`vOTU-ani`:** Minimum average nucleotide identity for fast clustering algorithm of viral contigs. (default: 95)
- **`vOTU-targetcov`:** Minimum target coverage for fast clustering algorithm of viral contigs. (default: 85)
- **`vOTU-querycov`:** Minimum query coverage for fast clustering algorithm of viral contigs. (default: 0)

## Outputs

```bash
identify/viral/output/derep
├── cluster_representatives.txt
├── clusters.tsv
└── combined.viralcontigs.derep.fa
```

The main output from this module is the assembly file `final.contigs.fa` which includes the final contigs generated by `megahit` or `SPAdes`. These contigs will be used for many steps in downstream analysis.
